definitions.available: Automatic analysis produced a complete, usable result for this section role or boundary event.
definitions.uncertain: Automatic analysis ran but produced a partial or ambiguous result (e.g., weak evidence, contradictory signals). The result is usable but not definitive.
definitions.unknown: Valid normal result — evidence is missing, weak, contradictory, or outside the vocabulary. No dummy confidence is invented.
definitions.unavailable: Automatic analysis was not run, not requested, or could not be started (e.g., missing downbeats, component not_run).
definitions.failed: Automatic analysis was requested and attempted but errored.

rules: Status applies independently to section roles and boundary events.
Boundary status and role status are separate fields; no shared universal confidence.
A neutral boundary may have status 'available' while the following section role has status 'unknown'.
A role status of 'available' does not imply the underlying neutral boundary status is 'available'.
Status 'unknown' is a first-class normal result, not an error or low-confidence placeholder.
No dummy confidence value is ever invented for 'unknown'.

automatic_result.description: Original analysis result emitted by the Arrangement Map classifier (#240). Preserved intact when overrides exist.

role.description: Automatically classified section role from the #238 vocabulary.

event.description: Automatically detected boundary event (separate from section role).

status.description: Status of the automatic analysis for this role or event.

evidence.description: Per-signal evidence contributions from #239 signals that were available.

positive_signals.description: Signal names from #239 that positively support this role/event.

negative_signals.description: Signal names from #239 that argue against this role/event.

missing_signals.description: Signal names from #239 that were nullable/unavailable for this section.

contradictory_signals.description: Signal names where positive and negative evidence both exist for different roles.

provenance.description: Source tracking for the automatic result.

scores.description: Optional per-role/event scores, only present when their semantics are explicitly defined. No universal confidence.

role_score.description: Track-relative role scoring value (e.g., weighted signal aggregate). Range and meaning defined by classifier implementation. Absent when not computable or not defined.

event_score.description: Track-relative boundary event scoring value. Range and meaning defined by classifier implementation. Absent when not computable or not defined.

boundary_quality.description: Neutral boundary quality from StructureV1 (#265), separate from role scoring. Range 0-1 (relative strength). Absent when not computable.

rules: Automatic result is never deleted or invisibly replaced by an override.
Both section role and boundary event automatic results are tracked separately.
Scores are optional and only included when their name, level (boundary/role/event), meaning, range, provenance, calibration status, and absent semantics are explicitly defined.
If scores are absent, no dummy values are invented.

manual_override.description: Explicit user correction applied to a section role or boundary event.

role.description: User-specified section role override. Optional if overriding only event.

event.description: User-specified boundary event override. Optional if overriding only role.

author.description: Override author identifier. Nullable when not reliably available in the runtime environment.

timestamp_utc.description: Override timestamp. Nullable when not reliably available.

reason.description: User-provided reason or note for the override. Nullable.

source.description: Fixed value 'manual' to distinguish from automatic analysis.

rules: Override applies to either section role OR boundary event OR both, independently.
Role override and event override are separate; they do not imply each other.
Metadata fields (author, timestamp, reason) are nullable — no fake values are generated when unavailable.
Override does not modify or delete the automatic result; both coexist.
An override with role='unknown' is valid and means the user explicitly asserts insufficient evidence.

effective_value_policy.description: How the effective (visible/used) value is determined from automatic result and manual override.
rules: If a valid manual override exists for a given layer (role or event), effective = manual override.
Otherwise, effective = automatic analysis result.
Automatic analysis result is always preserved and queryable.
Manual override is always preserved and queryable separately.
Effective value is a derived view, not a destructive replacement.
Role effective value and event effective value are computed independently.
Removing a manual override causes effective to fall back to automatic analysis automatically; no re-analysis is triggered.

B.description: Automatic groove + manual override to build

override.author: user1
override.reason: Energy rise feels like build not groove

C.description: Automatic drop preserved, effective becomes manual groove

D.description: drop_onset event separate from section role

override.reason: No sharp onset detected, gradual entry

E.description: Override removed → automatic becomes effective again

boundary_vs_role_uncertainty.description: Strict separation between neutral boundary certainty and arrangement role/event certainty.
rules: StructureV1 (#265) emits neutral boundaries with their own status (ok/partial/no_result/failed) and boundary_quality score (0-1 relative strength).
StructureV1 never emits roles or events (including drop_onset).
Arrangement Map (#240) emits section roles and boundary events with their own status (available/uncertain/unknown/unavailable/failed).
Arrangement Map never moves neutral boundaries.
drop_onset references a neutral boundary position; it does not create one.
A high boundary_quality does not imply a role status of 'available'.
A role status of 'available' does not imply the underlying neutral boundary had high boundary_quality.
Boundary status and role status are stored and queried independently.
No single universal confidence field bridges both layers.

score_confidence_policy.description: Rules for numerical scores/confidence values to prevent invented certainty.
rules: No universal 'confidence' field is defined or required.

Numerical scores are optional and only included when ALL of the following are explicitly defined: name, level (boundary/role/event), meaning, value range, provenance, calibration status (calibrated probability vs relative track score), and semantics of absent score.
If score semantics cannot be defined reliably, the score field is omitted entirely — no placeholder values.
Scores from different levels (boundary vs role vs event) are never combined into a single value.
Missing score never implies low confidence; it means 'not defined for this result'.
The 'evidence_completeness' signal from #239 accounts for missing/failed/weak/contradictory inputs instead of inventing a confidence number.

major_increments: Automatic result or manual override field structure changes
minor_increments: Non-breaking JSON additions (new optional fields with defaults)

acceptance_mapping.compatible_with_238_239_240_265: Cross-references in header + field enums matching #238 vocabulary
